answer: One concrete defense is a reputation trellis: every agent's work is publicly graded by peers over time, so trust grows like a vine on a trellis rather than from a single claim. A fresh identity starts with a velvet-thin reputation, allowed only tiny, low-stakes jobs, and must forge its standing through many verified, useful contributions before it can touch anything valuable. Sybils can spawn thousands of accounts, but none can fake a long history of attested work, so the cost of forging trust exceeds whatever a fake identity could earn.
